overview: The update-health packet is server-authored, so anticheats cannot see a client-spoofed health value; what they can see is the server's own health bookkeeping around it. Modern anticheats parse WrapperPlayServerUpdateHealth on the send side to track death and food state (Grim, BetterAnticheat), while regen and god-mode checks watch EntityRegainHealthEvent and damage events to catch fast-heal and damage suppression (Negativity, Arc, NoCheatPlus, Daedalus, ThotPatrol, MIU). The packet itself is never flagged; it is the reference clock for health-related checks.

checks.name: UpdateHealth death tracking (BetterAnticheat)
checks.purpose: Track the client-visible death state from the update-health payload and the client's own respawn acknowledgement.
checks.how_it_works: PlayerStatusTracker.handlePacketPlaySend wraps UPDATE_HEALTH as WrapperPlayServerUpdateHealth and, inside a confirmation transaction, pushes isDead = (health == 0) into a ten-slot BooleanManyState that flushes only after the client confirms the packet. The receive side mirrors it: a CLIENT_STATUS PERFORM_RESPAWN pushes isDead = false and flushes four slots at once, deliberately wiping stale death states to defeat disablers that delay selected responses.
checks.detects: Death-state desync: a client that selectively delays packet responses to hide its own death or respawn timing from the anticheat.
checks.variations: Grim does the same tracking in PacketPlayerRespawn: it stores lastHealth, lastFood and lastSaturation, marks the simulated self entity dead when health reaches zero and feeds BadPacketsM.onDeath; Artemis mirrors health into its emulator through BntityPlayerSP.setPlayerSPHealth.

checks.name: Regen (Negativity)
checks.purpose: Flag fast regeneration: health regaining faster than the version's natural regen interval allows.
checks.how_it_works: RegenProtocol.onRegen listens to EntityRegainHealthEvent for players. It skips players with active regen-affecting potions, records the time between regains and flags when the gap is below the version's timeBetweenTwoRegen plus ping (per-version table in Version). A gap under 50 ms plus ping is a hard violation, and the event is cancelled when setbacks are enabled. The protocol also tags the player's flying reason on golden-apple interactions so movement checks can discount regen-based vertical motion.
checks.detects: Auto-regen modules and fast-heal packets that produce health regains faster than the per-version interval tables permit.
checks.variations: Arc-v2 Regeneration compares the last health event against a configurable regen-time (3400 ms default); Daedalus Regen and ThotPatrol BadPacketsA use the same SATIATED-reason timing pattern; MIU FastHealA computes the expected interval from the player's health level and regen potion stage.

checks.name: Regeneration (Arc v2)
checks.purpose: Classic satiated-regen rate check: health must not regenerate faster than the configured interval.
checks.how_it_works: FightListener.onRegen records the SATIATED regain timestamp into FightData when the check can run; Regeneration.check computes now minus lastHealthEvent and fails when the gap is below the regen-time value read from the check config (3400 ms default). It is one of the smallest checks in the corpus: a timestamp, a subtraction and a threshold.
checks.detects: Fast-regen modules that exploit the satiated regeneration mechanic.
checks.variations: Negativity RegenProtocol adds per-version tables and potion exemptions; Daedalus Regen and ThotPatrol BadPacketsA count packets between regains; NoCheatPlus tracks regainHealthTime in FightData and feeds it into GodMode's expectation model.

checks.name: GodMode (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Detect players that ignore inflicted damage or keep an impossible health ceiling across regen and damage events.
checks.how_it_works: GodMode.check runs on damage events against FightData bookkeeping: regainHealthTime is stamped by FightListener.onEntityRegainHealth, godModeHealth tracks the highest health the player has held, and the check flags when current health stays above the expected post-damage value or when no damage lands despite a hit. The regain-tracking variant is what the corpus shows; the original 2012-era sensitivity path is marked as likely obsolete in the source.
checks.detects: God-mode exploits, damage suppression and health-ceiling manipulation around combat.
checks.variations: Kauri HealthSpoof is the modern replacement pattern; MIU AntiDamageA compares post-damage health against the expected drop; Daedalus Regen watches only the regain rate.
